questions.question: What does an aesthetic predictor score represent?
options: A model-version-specific estimate learned from particular preference labels
Universal artistic quality
Copyright permission
Image-caption factual correctness
questions.explanation: The score inherits the predictor architecture, embedding model, training labels, raters, and calibration; it is not a universal truth.

questions.question: Why should image-text alignment, aesthetics, safety, and provenance remain separate fields?
options: Each signal answers a different question and can fail independently
A composite score is always larger
Separate fields eliminate model bias
Only provenance affects model behavior
questions.explanation: A pair can be aligned but unsafe, aesthetically preferred but wrongly captioned, or well scored without sufficient rights evidence.

questions.question: A URL serves different bytes than it did when scored. What should the pipeline do?
options: Reuse the old scores because the URL is unchanged
Treat the new content hash as a new candidate and rescore it
Overwrite the old hash in every manifest
Skip decode and hash validation
questions.explanation: Scores and decisions must bind to exact content identity, not a mutable locator.

questions.question: What does a large slice-retention gap after filtering indicate?
options: The aggregate retained count may hide concentrated exclusion of a content shape
The dataset is automatically unsafe
All slices have equal representation
The CLIP model is perfectly calibrated
questions.explanation: Before/after slice analysis is needed because a healthy total can coexist with complete loss of modalities, languages, or source types.

questions.question: Why are scorer and preprocessing versions part of every score record?
options: To reproduce prior releases and compare decision changes after rescoring
To make URLs immutable
To grant legal permission
To remove the need for human review
questions.explanation: Changing a model or preprocessing path can move scores and thresholds; versioned records preserve lineage.

questions.question: What should happen when a reviewed removal request affects released shards?
options: Update only the current user interface
Trace affected manifests, publish successors, propagate removal, and block re-entry
Delete all audit evidence
Keep the pair because it passed an aesthetic threshold
questions.explanation: A governed dataset needs downstream lineage and a durable restricted-identity path, not only pre-release filtering.

questions.question: What does recorded source provenance prove by itself?
options: Where the candidate came from and what evidence was recorded, not necessarily permission to train
Consent from every depicted person
That the caption is accurate
That the pair is safe
questions.explanation: Provenance supports review and traceability; legal basis, consent, and policy suitability require separate evidence and decisions.
